findings.finding: F1: R2 puts the first Legion-specific policy into packages/envoy, a generic issue tracker that today knows nothing about a `legion` label; the spec names neither the field nor where the behaviour is documented.
findings.answer: The plan implements the approved design with a boolean `legion_managed_status` and the label name hard-coded as the daemon hard-codes it (packages/daemon/internal/dispatch/types.go:53), updates both claim route descriptions in api/routes_table.go:86-87, and names the field's name and the generic-server coupling as the architect's call in the plan's 'For the architect' section and in the completion report.

findings.finding: F2: the spec says only 'the claim response carries one more field'; model.Issue is embedded in model.IssueEventPayload, so a field added inside it enters every issue event, and the dashboard merges the release body into its issue cache.
findings.answer: Task 2 answers with a Go wrapper that embeds model.Issue and adds the one field, so the JSON stays flat and no event payload, no Go test decode and no dashboard merge changes. The plan states the precedent (model.IssueRouteReach, model.go:224-231) and the dashboard consumer (IssueHeader.tsx:167-170).

findings.finding: F3: the two existing parent-walk precedents disagree at the depth cap — issueComponentsLateral stops silently, issueRepoLateral refuses the read — and the spec picks neither.
findings.answer: Task 2 answers 'no Legion issue above you' at the cap and the plan records why that is unreachable: a claim calls loadIssue, whose repoScan.resolve already refuses a chain deeper than 32 links (api/issue_repo.go:94-98), so the claim fails before the new walk runs. The walk runs inside claimWrite's transaction under the issue's row lock, and compares labels case-insensitively because labels keep their typed case (normalizeIssueLabels, issue_queries.go:166-185).

findings.finding: F5: relaxing the validation does not let an inner ref edit the spec (innerRefProblem judges the ref's kind), but the spec's claim that the hint at dispatch-execute.ts:1017-1021 'stays true' is false, and that hint must be reworded.
findings.answer: Task 3 rewords the comment and the ownerArguments branch so the hint still names the artifact for dispatch_suggest and no longer claims doc-edit refuses an issue alone, and updates dispatch-execute.test.ts:563-575. Recorded as the third spec departure.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance: "Each of the four is proven through the `dispatch` command an agent actually runs, against a Dispatch server running from this change (`bun run dispatch:local` starts one, seeded and signed in), not only through unit tests of the pieces."
specDepartures.plan: The server is started with `packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh` against a rootless pgvector Postgres assembled in the pod, and the `dispatch` command is the branch's own build (`packages/pi-envoy/bin/dispatch` after `bun run build`), not the plugin copy on PATH.
specDepartures.evidence: run-server.sh builds and execs the same Go server from the working tree and needs only DATABASE_URL, go, openssl, flock. local-instance.ts:118-139 additionally runs `bun run build:web` and the whole Playwright listener set, and that web build has a known pod failure mode (docs/solutions/testing/the-real-dispatch-stack-runs-inside-a-legion-pod-with-no-postgres-no-docker-and-no-root-INFRA-42.md, step 4). Measured in this pod on 2026-10-24: no docker, no psql, no C compiler; `kubectl auth can-i create services` and `get services` both answer no, so docs/kubernetes.md's in-cluster Job route is closed.

acceptance: Each of the four is proven through the `dispatch` command an agent actually runs, against a Dispatch server running from this change (`bun run dispatch:local` starts one, seeded and signed in), not only through unit tests of the pieces.

specDepartures.spec: Goals: "Goal: each text an agent gets after a write is true for that agent."
specDepartures.plan: The plan builds R1, R2 and R3 only. A fourth text reached by that Goal is left out: after any write to an issue still in triage the client appends "<KEY> is still in triage - nobody can see its development status. See the `dispatch` skill, 'Issue status is yours to move'.", which on a Legion issue contradicts that same skill section.
specDepartures.evidence: packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-execute.ts:267-277 renders that line for every write; skills/dispatch/SKILL.md:95 says "Never write the status of an issue with the `legion` label or under one." Including it would move the ancestor label walk from the claim path into computeWriteAdvice (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/write_advice.go:57-110), which runs on every message, comment and ask.

outcome.scope: The triage advice line is not changed by this issue; whether the spec takes it is the architect's decision.
